stories.summary: A schoolteacher diagnosed with melanoma provides an inside look at what it was like to be treated with a cancer vaccine developed by Merck and Moderna.

stories.title: Forty percent of high school students report binge eating in new CDC survey
stories.summary: About 40% of high school students reported binge-eating in the past month in a new CDC survey, highlighting how widespread this form of disordered eating is among young people.

stories.title: Hospital doctors to strike as pay dispute continues
stories.summary: The British Medical Association says hospital doctors in Northern Ireland plan to strike in November.

stories.summary: Rep. Jake Auchincloss (D-Mass.) has some advice for fellow lawmakers: unapologetically support the biotech industry.

stories.title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says
stories.summary: New guidance says trans patients should be cared for on single-sex hospital wards or bays that align with their biological sex.

stories.title: Trump administration advances plan for peptide drugs favored by RFK Jr.
stories.summary: U.S. health officials are moving ahead with a plan to allow specialty pharmacies to produce certain peptides, a class of largely unregulated injections favored by health secretary Robert F. Kennedy…

stories.title: Ukraine: Critical health supplies destroyed in ongoing Russian attacks
stories.summary: Ongoing and deadly Russian attacks across Ukraine are causing serious healthcare disruption, with more than $1.5 million-worth of medicines and supplies destroyed in four separate strikes on warehouses used by the UN there since July.

stories.title: WHO urges vigilance after Kenya confirms second Ebola case
stories.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) continues to support Kenya’s efforts to contain Ebola after a second person tested positive for the Bundibugyo virus, the UN agency’s representative in the country said on Thursday.

stories.title: DR Congo: Cholera cases spike amid fight against Ebola
stories.summary: The cholera epidemic continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 125,000 suspected cases and 3,644 suspected deaths were recorded between January 2025 and the end of September 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Wednesday.

stories.title: Former FDA officials blast DOGE as ‘one of the biggest disasters in American history’
stories.summary: Three former FDA chiefs criticized the DOGE cuts to the agency, saying they robbed the FDA of institutional knowledge that will take years to restore.

stories.title: Health workers tackle taboos over drinking with new AI tool
stories.summary: A new AI-powered hub for health professionals aims to help identify alcohol-related risks and launch discussions with patients, including the link between drinking and cancer, the World Health Organization (WHO) announced on Wednesday.

stories.title: How consumer tech company Whoop is building for Medicare patients

stories.title: Poisoned Air and Blood: Pakistan Confronts a Hidden Lead Crisis Fed by Its Toxic Skies

stories.summary: Factory workers in India are being asked to wear GoPro cameras to record the way they do their jobs. The ultimate goal is to train robots to take over. Will it work?

stories.title: WHO calls for urgent health action across the Eastern Mediterranean
stories.summary: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) has called for promoting, providing and protecting health in the Eastern Mediterranean region, home to some of the world’s top humanitarian crises such as Sudan, Yemen and the Occupied Palestinian Territory.

stories.title: The Crisis That Didn’t Happen: One Health Has the Arguments; It Needs the Budget
stories.summary: Six years after COVID-19, with Ebola Bundibugyo virus still raging in eastern Congo and the pandemic treaty stalled, a packed World Health Summit workshop asked why the world keeps paying for fire engines instead of fire prevention.

stories.title: With Only Three ‘No’ Votes, UN Adopts Political Declaration on Pandemic Preparedness
stories.summary: The United Nations General Assembly adopted the Political Declaration on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness, and Response (PPPR) by a substantial majority at a plenary meeting in New York on Monday, with 153 countries voting in favor and only three against.

stories.title: Americans trust science more than peers around the world, survey shows
